hints: Focus on the second step first, what functional group change happens when product X becomes 1-methylcyclohexanol?
Notice the first step is addition of HBr to 1-methylcyclohexene, so Markovnikov addition puts Br on the more substituted carbon to give 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane.
To turn that tertiary bromoalkane into an alcohol you need substitution of Br by OH, so think about which reagent supplies $OH^-$ for substitution rather than elimination or oxidation.
walkthrough:
**Work out what product X is**

Think of HBr adding across the C=C bond. The H adds first to make the most stable carbocation.

For 1-methylcyclohexene, $H^+$ adds to the $CH$ carbon to leave a tertiary carbocation on the $C(CH_3)$ carbon, then $Br^-$ attacks there. So X is 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane:
$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)C=CH- + HBr} \rightarrow \text{(CH}_3\text{)C(Br)-CH}_2\text{-}$$

**Work out what change is needed in step 2**

Compare X with the final product. The carbon skeleton is the same, only $Br$ is replaced by $OH$ on the same tertiary carbon.

$$\text{1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane} \rightarrow \text{1-methylcyclohexanol}$$
This is nucleophilic substitution of a halogenoalkane to form an alcohol.

**Choose the reagent for substitution**

Substitution by $OH^-$ needs aqueous sodium hydroxide with heat. Water acts as solvent and $OH^-$ acts as nucleophile.

Ethanolic NaOH would cause elimination back to the alkene, and $KMnO_4$ would oxidise, not substitute. So reagent Y must be aqueous NaOH.

options.A: Aqueous NaOH provides $OH^-$ as a nucleophile for hydrolysis. Heating the tertiary bromide X with aqueous NaOH gives nucleophilic substitution of $Br$ by $OH$ to form 1-methylcyclohexanol. This is the standard halogenoalkane to alcohol route.
options.B: Cold dilute $KMnO_4$ is for mild oxidation of alkenes to diols, not for substitution of a bromoalkane. Product X has no C=C bond left to oxidise, so this reagent would not give the desired alcohol.
options.C: Ethanolic NaOH favours elimination, not substitution. It would remove HBr from X to reform 1-methylcyclohexene. This is the classic aqueous versus ethanolic trap: aqueous gives substitution to alcohol, ethanolic gives elimination to alkene.
options.D: Hot concentrated $KMnO_4$ is a strong oxidising agent that cleaves C=C bonds or oxidises side chains. It does not convert $C-Br$ to $C-OH$, and would destroy the ring system rather than give clean substitution.
